title: MPRIS as the media integration, with app-side player arbitration
context: Windows exposes a single 'current session' through SMTC. Linux players each export org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.Player at the same object path, so there is no system-provided notion of which player is active.
options: MPRIS over D-Bus with our own active-player selection
Read player state through PipeWire only (no transport control)
proposal: One zbus MessageStream for PropertiesChanged and NameOwnerChanged, plus explicit arbitration: pinned player, else most recently active playing player, else most recently active paused player.
decision: MPRIS with app-side arbitration and periodic discovery reconciliation every ~3 s, so a missed bus signal cannot leave a dead player on screen.
consequences: Players that do not implement optional MPRIS members degrade per capability (CanPlay/CanGoNext/CanSeek...).
No queue look-ahead is available, so the Next-Up flyout cannot be reproduced.
Transport actions are only offered when the player advertises the capability.
